Democrats continue to have an edge over Republicans in vote intent for the November elections for U.S. Congress, according to the latest Economist / YouGov Poll. 46% of registered voters say they will vote for the Democratic Party candidate in their district, and 40% will vote for the Republican candidate. That 6-point Democratic lead among registered voters is in line with recent weeks, and larger than the Democrats' low-single-digit lead for much of the summer. # How Trump’s Approval Rating Has Changed With White Voters This Summer

Published

Sep 02, 2026 at 10:24 PM EDT

Alex Backus

Editor

President Donald Trump's approval rating among white voters has fallen 7 percentage points since the beginning of the summer, according to ActiVote polling, as other surveys have also pointed to weakening views of the president among a group central to his electoral coalition. [...] Among white Americans without college degrees, 43 percent approved of Trump's job performance while 52 percent disapproved. According to YouGov, Trump's three-poll average net approval among the group stood at -6, down from plus 27 during the first three weeks of his second term.
